title: FP8/INT8 calibration impact on function-calling structured output: schema conformance evaluation
creator: Marcus Li
description: Run an end-to-end evaluation that measures how FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles and our calibration workflows affect the correctness of structured outputs used for function calling. Focus on JSON schema conformance, field type fidelity, and downstream function-invocation success rate. Produce actionable calibration/quant profile recommendations and a regression gating signal for CI.
background: We have anecdotal reports of increased schema parsing errors and mis-typed fields when models are served with aggressive quantization profiles (FP8 and some INT8 kernels). Existing post-calibration checks focus on token-level perplexity and aggregate LM logits, but we lack a targeted pipeline that validates structured outputs against JSON schemas and simulates downstream function calling to measure practical correctness.
goal: 1) Quantify schema conformance delta vs FP32 baseline for FP8 and INT8 profiles across a representative function-calling prompt suite. 2) Augment the calibration workflow with schema-aware metrics and recommend per-model quant profiles (or fallbacks) based on acceptable thresholds. 3) Add automated regression checks in PR CI that block profiles causing >2% absolute drop in schema-pass rate for high-priority prompts.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a new test harness that runs model variants (FP32 baseline, FP8-calibrated, INT8-calibrated) on an expanding suite of structured-output prompts and verifies output against target JSON schemas using a tolerant checker (type coercion rules, required/optional fields). 2) Instrument function-call simulator to attempt RPC invocation on parsed outputs and record invocation success/failure. 3) Extend calibration job artifacts to emit 'schema calibration report' including per-field error heatmaps and suggested bias/scale adjustments. 4) Integrate results into the Console rollout dashboard and add CI gating rules referencing the schema-pass metric.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness runs FP32, FP8, INT8 variants end-to-end and produces a JSON summary report for each model variant
Schema-pass rate metric defined and computed: percentage of outputs that validate and parse unambiguously into the expected function call payload
Baseline (FP32) and quantized deltas measured for 3 representative workloads: dialog tool-calls, structured API generation, and embedding metadata outputs
If a quant profile causes >2% absolute drop in schema-pass rate for high-priority prompt set, CI gating rule fails (configurable threshold)
Calibration report suggests at least one actionable mitigation per failing model (fallback profile, additional calibration steps, prompt templates)
test_plan: Curate a corpus of ~2k prompts across 6 schemas: payment_initiate, calendar_create, search_query, product_spec, anonymize_payload, rerank_instruction
Run each prompt 3x across seeds for FP32 baseline, FP8 profile A/B, INT8 profile canonical using current quant kernels
Validation: strict JSON Schema (Draft 7) validation + tolerant parser that records type coercions and missing fields
Function-call simulator executes parsed payloads against mocked endpoints and classifies outcomes: success, recoverable_error, fatal_error
Compute metrics: schema_pass_rate, field_type_mismatch_rate, parse_error_rate, function_invocation_success_rate, latency and token budget impact
Store per-prompt diffs and heatmaps to S3 and surface in Console QA dashboard for triage
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Calibration noise produces flakey pass/fail at low sample sizes — Mitigation: increase evaluation repeats and use bootstrap CI on metrics
Risk: JSON schema strictness may flag benign formatting differences — Mitigation: define canonical tolerance rules and separate hard vs soft failures
Risk: Evaluation runtime is long for full corpus across many models — Mitigation: staged evaluations with quick smoke set for CI and nightly full run
Risk: Instrumentation pulls in infra changes (ENG-7221) — Mitigation: mock kernels in unit tests and run integration once kernels are available
notes: Design decision: prefer reporting structured deltas and recommended mitigations rather than automatic profile rollbacks to avoid overreaction to noisy signals
Trade-off: FP8 gives significant cost wins but may require schema-aware calibration heuristics; accept up to 1.5% drop for non-critical schemas with console flagging
We will prioritize 3 high-impact customer schemas for stricter thresholds (payment_initiate, calendar_create, product_spec)
Follow-up: consider augmenting calibration objective with a lightweight schema-likelihood loss term if manual mitigations are insufficient
